title: Portfolio
text:
A selection of some of my research and academic projects.


The Contexts That Bind Us: Networks, Multiplexity, and Embeddedness in Institutional Domains
Master’s Thesis · Leiden University & CBS (Statistics Netherlands) · 2026
This thesis examines how the organisation of social ties across institutional domains relates to generalised trust in the Netherlands. Using the CBS Person Network, a whole-population multilayer network covering approximately 17 million Dutch residents across five institutional domains (family, household, neighbourhood, workplace, and education), I developed two individual-level dimensions of cross-domain embeddedness. Multiplexity captures whether the same individuals are connected across multiple domains, whereas participation evenness captures how evenly ties are distributed across domains. A key measurement contribution was an adjusted multiplexity measure that accounts for administrative overlap between family and household registers. Person-level measures were linked to the Social Cohesion and Well-being Survey (2020–2023, N = 28,483) to examine their association with generalised trust.
 Thesis ·  Conference Abstract



Immigration to Europe: An Interactive Dashboard
EMOS Presentation of Official Statistics · Leiden University · 2025
An interactive Shiny application that visualises immigration patterns across European countries using Eurostat data. The dashboard includes time-series views by country, choropleth maps of immigration counts, and maps showing immigration as a share of the national population. Data were sourced from the Eurostat migration (migr_imm8) and population (demo_pjan) databases, combined with NUTS-0 boundary files for spatial visualisation.
 Live app  Code



Housing Price Statistics in Den Bosch
EMOS Statistical Production Systems · Leiden University · 2025
This project implements a reproducible statistical production pipeline for computing average housing prices in Den Bosch. Using synthetic data from the Dutch buildings register and property sales records, the pipeline follows a five-stage workflow from raw data ingestion through preprocessing, validation, and statistical processing to final output. Each stage is modular and documented, reflecting the production system standards taught in the European Master in Official Statistics (EMOS) programme.
 Code



Social Factors Influencing Children’s Pro-Environmental Behaviour
Statistical Consulting Project · Leiden University · 2024
This study investigated how social factors influence pro-environmental behaviour (PEB) in children and adolescents aged 9 to 15 years. Participants (N = 164) from 13 classrooms across two schools completed an effort-based choice task across self, climate, and prosocial targets. We used generalized linear mixed-effects models to examine whether experimentally manipulated social norm messages affect effortful pro-environmental behaviour, and whether individual social susceptibility and classroom cohesion moderated these effects.

Developed an adjusted multiplexity measure to correct for administrative overlap between family and household registers, and linked a whole-population multilayer network (~17 million Dutch residents) to survey data (\(N\) = 28,483) to examine how the organisation of social ties across institutional domains relates to generalised trust.

title: Milena Costa
text:
Hi! I’m Milena, a quantitative social scientist. I grew up in Brazil and moved to Belgium when I was eighteen, where I spent two years as an au pair, learning Dutch at the KU Leuven. Watching children grow up in a different context than my own made me curious about how the environments we grow up in shape who we become. I have been in the Netherlands for five years now, and am currently based in Leiden.
Through a bachelor’s in Psychology at Maastricht University, I learned to think about behaviour in context. I also discovered a passion for the quantitative side of research, especially the challenge of measuring things that aren’t directly observable, like well-being or social relationships. A master’s in Statistics and Data Science gave me a stronger foundation in statistical modelling, research design, and working with complex data. For my master’s thesis at Statistics Netherlands (CBS), I used a whole-population network of the Netherlands to investigate how people’s embeddedness in different social domains, such as work, neighbourhood, and household, relates to generalised trust. I enjoy applying quantitative methods to answer relevant social questions, and questioning what the patterns I find actually mean in people’s daily lives.
I am looking to continue working in applied statistics, answering questions about how social contexts shape individual outcomes. Methodologically, I am particularly interested in measurement and psychometrics, multilevel and longitudinal modelling, and social network analysis.
Outside of research, you’ll find me taking care of my tropical plants and having deep discussions about the meaning of life. I love learning about new cultures, exploring different perspectives, watching art house films, and going down rabbit holes about whatever has caught my attention lately. Whenever I get the chance, I also like to scuba dive.
